docs.title: vexy-dexypy
docs.text:
vexy-dexypy turns a web page into slide decks. It takes one URL or local HTML file, works out where the slides inside the page should break, and renders the page to PDF through several engines in parallel. Each engine writes its own folder of single-page PDFs. You compare the folders and build your final deck from the best version of each slide.

No two engines paginate a page the same way. A Webflow hero often looks best through Chromium, while a documentation page often looks best through a CSS paged-media engine. vexy-dexypy runs the engines side by side and leaves the choice to you.

docs.title: What goes in, what comes out
docs.text:
Input An http:// or https:// URL, or a path to a local .html file. Output A folder per page under out/, with one sub-folder per rendering strategy and a _meta/ folder that records the slide plan and the run summary.

For vexy-dexypy build https://www.vexy.art/lines/ the result looks like this (the folder name is a slug derived from the URL):

out/www-vexy-art-lines/
  raw/            index.html                 # the fetched page
  normalized/     normalized.html            # slide-shaped sections
  playwright/     01-slide.pdf  02-slide.pdf  …  index.html
  reveal/         01-slide.pdf  …  index.html
  vivliostyle/    01-slide.pdf  …  index.html
  _meta/          page.json  slideplan.json  run-summary.json

A strategy that fails becomes a warning in the summary table. The run still writes the decks that worked.

docs.title: The six stages
docs.text:
1. Read: fetch the page (or copy the local file).
  2. Analyze: recognize the page builder (Webflow, MkDocs Material, and others) and plan slide breaks at the target stage size.
  3. Normalize: restructure the DOM into slide-shaped <section> elements, in the browser, with the bundled vexy-dexyjs preprocessor.
  4. Prepare: write the paged-media CSS, reveal.js, impress.js or Marp wrapping that each engine expects.
  5. Render: export a combined PDF through every selected engine.
  6. Write: split each PDF into numbered single-page files, optionally convert them to SVG, and write an HTML preview.

Architecture follows one page through every stage.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Installation: Python, Chromium and the optional engines.
  • Quick start: your first build, step by step.
  • Command line: every command and flag.
  • Configuration: vexy-dexypy.toml keys and precedence.
  • Engines: what each strategy does and what it needs.
  • Extending: add readers, importers or exporters as plugins.
  • Troubleshooting: common failures and fixes.
  • Contributing: development setup, tests and releases.

docs.title: Licence
docs.text: See the LICENSE file in the repository. Some engines vexy-dexypy can call have their own licences: Vivliostyle is AGPL and Prince is proprietary. vexy-dexypy runs them as separate programs and does not link them.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
vexy-dexypy is a six-stage pipeline. Stages 1 to 3 run once per page. Stages 4 to 6 run once per strategy. Stages pass typed objects from vexy_dexypy.model to each other and write JSON sidecars, so a later stage can run again without the earlier ones.

This page follows one build through the stages:

vexy-dexypy build https://www.vexy.art/lines/ --strategies playwright,reveal

docs.title: Stage 1: read
docs.text:
Input: a Source. Source.parse sets kind to url for http:// and https:// input, and to file for anything else, and computes the slug www-vexy-art-lines.

The reader (vexy_dexypy.readers.read) chooses a reader from the fetch mode:

  • Local files: StaticReader.
  • offline: OfflineReader, which runs single-file or monolith.
  • live (default): LiveReader, if Playwright is installed.
  • Otherwise: the registered reader with the highest can_read score. The static reader scores 0.5, the dynamic reader 0.3.

Output: a PageDoc with the captured HTML at out/www-vexy-art-lines/raw/index.html, the asset folder, a content hash, and metadata (title, generator).

The page is then classified. classify lowercases the HTML and counts fingerprint strings per page type:

Page type Fingerprints webflow data-wf-page, w-mod-js, data-w-id, webflow.js mkdocs-material mkdocs-material, md-content, data-md-component, md-typeset docusaurus __docusaurus, theme-doc-markdown framer data-framer-name, framer.app bubble data-bb-id, bubble-element

One hit gives confidence 0.5; each extra hit adds 0.25, up to 1.0. The highest confidence wins; no hits means generic. The result is written to _meta/page.json.

docs.title: Stage 2: analyze
docs.text:
paginate.analyze opens the HTML in Chromium at the stage size (1280×720 by default) and measures every section, article, h1, h2, h3, img, .card and [class*="hero"] element. plan_breaks walks the visible elements from top to bottom:

  • An element taller than the stage adds breaks every stage height inside it (reason overflow).
  • An element that starts more than one stage height (less 50 px) below the current slide start adds a break at its top (reason overflow).
  • An h1, h2, section or article that starts more than 40% of a stage height below the current slide start adds a break (reason is the tag name).

Breaks are sorted and duplicates within 1 px are removed. The slide count is the number of breaks plus one.

Without Playwright, a static fallback adds one evenly spaced advisory break per <section> or <h2> and marks the plan {"mode": "static-fallback"}.

With --vision, a full-page screenshot is sent to the vision model, and its y values are added as vision breaks. The merged breaks are de-duplicated within 10% of the stage height. If the model is unreachable, the heuristic plan is kept.

Output: a SlidePlan, written to _meta/slideplan.json.

docs.title: Stage 3: normalize
docs.text:
pick_importer chooses the importer whose name matches the page type, or the generic importer. Every importer first tries the in-browser preprocessor: it injects the bundled vexy-dexyjs.js into the page and calls window.VexyDexy.preprocess(config) with the framework name, stage size and breaks. The returned HTML is a sequence of <section> slides.

If the browser step fails, each importer has a Python fallback:

  • webflow: keeps <section> elements that are not menu, nav, footer, mask, header or banner chrome, and tags each one light or dark from its background colour. With fewer than two sections, it removes chrome and distributes the page blocks into the planned slide count.
  • mkdocs-material: removes the Material header, sidebars, navigation and footer, and splits article.md-content__inner at h1 and h2.
  • generic: extracts the article body with trafilatura if installed, otherwise strips nav, header, footer, aside, script and style, then splits at headings.
  • docusaurus: removes page chrome and splits .theme-doc-markdown.
  • bubble: changes position: absolute inline styles to position: relative, then hands the page to the generic importer.
  • framer: hands the page to the generic importer.

Output: out/www-vexy-art-lines/normalized/normalized.html. Asset references are rewritten from assets/ to ../raw/assets/ so they still resolve.

docs.title: Stage 4: prepare
docs.text:
preexport.prepare creates out/www-vexy-art-lines/playwright/ and out/www-vexy-art-lines/reveal/, writes _paged.css and _theme.css into each, and builds the engine input for the strategy's chassis (paged, reveal, impress or marp). See Engines.

Output: a RenderJob per strategy.

docs.title: Stage 5: render
docs.text:
The orchestrator runs the two strategies concurrently. Each exporter writes _combined.pdf, and a copy goes to _meta/cache/.

Local pages are never opened as file://. A short-lived HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 serves the folder two levels above the HTML file, so ../raw/assets/ links, web fonts, fetch() calls and ES modules behave as on a real site. Navigation waits for the load event and then pauses 400 ms.

docs.title: Stage 6: write
docs.text:
writers.write_deck splits _combined.pdf with pypdf into 01-slide.pdf, 02-slide.pdf, …, optionally converts them to SVG, and writes index.html. The orchestrator then writes _meta/run-summary.json:

{
  "source": "https://www.vexy.art/lines/",
  "framework": "webflow",
  "slides": 12,
  "results": [
    {"strategy": "playwright", "ok": true, "slides": 11, "error": null},
    {"strategy": "reveal", "ok": true, "slides": 9, "error": null}
  ]
}

The numbers in this example are illustrative.

docs.title: Error types
docs.text:
All errors derive from VexyDexError in vexy_dexypy.errors:

Error Raised when UsageError A flag or config value is invalid (exit code 1) ReadError Fetching, archiving or reading the source fails NormalizeError A normalizer fails ExportError An engine fails; isolated to its strategy WriteError Splitting or SVG conversion fails; isolated to its strategy VisionError The vision model is unavailable or returns unusable data

docs.title: Source layout
docs.text:
src/vexy_dexypy/
  cli.py            # Fire commands
  settings.py       # flags + TOML -> frozen Settings
  model.py          # Source, PageDoc, Break, SlidePlan, Strategy, RenderJob, DeckResult
  orchestrator.py   # stage sequencing and concurrency
  classify.py       # page-type fingerprints
  paginate.py       # slide-break planning
  vision.py         # optional vision refinement
  dom.py            # shared BeautifulSoup helpers
  preexport.py      # CSS and deck wrapping
  writers.py        # split, SVG, preview
  _browser.py       # loopback server, browser launch, vexy-dexyjs injection
  readers/  importers/  exporters/
  assets/           # vexy-dexyjs.js, reveal.js, impress.js

The full design is in the 24-chapter specification in the repository's spec/ folder.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
The vexy-dexypy command is built with Python Fire. It has five commands. You can also run it as python -m vexy_dexypy.

vexy-dexypy build URL [flags]
vexy-dexypy read URL [flags]
vexy-dexypy analyze URL [flags]
vexy-dexypy render SLUG STRATEGY [flags]
vexy-dexypy split PDF [flags]

Show the help for any command with --help, for example vexy-dexypy build --help.

Tip

Fire accepts flag names with underscores (--no_cache) or hyphens (--no-cache). If Fire mistakes a flag value for a positional argument, put the flags after a -- separator.

docs.title: build
docs.text:
Runs the whole pipeline: read, analyze, normalize, prepare, render and write, for every selected strategy.

Flag Default Meaning URL (required) http(s):// URL or local HTML file path --out out Output root folder --aspect none (720p) Stage profile: 720p, 1080p or 810p --size none Stage size as WxH, for example 1600x900; overrides --aspect --strategies all Comma-separated strategy names, or all --svg False Also convert each slide PDF to SVG --vision False Refine slide breaks with a local vision model --verbose False Log at DEBUG level instead of INFO --no_cache False Ignore cached engine PDFs and render again --browser_engine none (playwright) playwright, playwrightauthor or cloakbrowser --fetch_mode none (live) live, localize or offline

Flags left unset fall back to the configuration file, then to the built-in default. See Configuration.

docs.title: Fetch modes
docs.text:
live The default. Opens the URL in the browser, captures the rendered DOM, and adds a <base href> that points at the page's own address. Fonts, CSS and images keep loading from the network. If Playwright is not installed, the run falls back to localize. localize Fetches the HTML with httpx and downloads every <link>, <script>, <img> and <source> asset into raw/assets/, including url() and @import targets inside stylesheets. If the fetched body has fewer than 500 characters of text, the static reader treats the page as client-rendered and re-reads it in headless Chromium. offline Runs an external archiver (single-file by default, or monolith) to produce one self-contained HTML file. If the archiver is not on PATH, the run falls back to localize.

Local files always use the static reader, whatever the fetch mode.

docs.title: Browser engines
docs.text:
playwright Standard Playwright Chromium. The default. playwrightauthor Imports playwrightauthor from private/playwrightauthor/src (relative to the current folder) for persistent browser sessions. cloakbrowser Uses the cloakbrowser package to launch a headless browser.

The browser engine applies to the live reader and to the in-browser vexy-dexyjs preprocessing. The exporters always launch Playwright Chromium.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 At least one strategy succeeded 1 Usage error, for example an unknown strategy or a malformed --size 2 No strategy succeeded, no strategy ran, or another vexy-dexypy error stopped the run

docs.title: read
docs.text:
Runs stage 1 only. It fetches the page, classifies it, writes _meta/page.json, and prints the path of the captured HTML.

Flags: --out, --verbose, --browser_engine, --fetch_mode.

vexy-dexypy read https://www.vexy.art/lines/

docs.title: analyze
docs.text:
Runs stages 1 and 2. It writes _meta/page.json and _meta/slideplan.json, then prints the slide count and the break offsets in pixels.

Flags: --out, --aspect, --size, --vision, --verbose, --browser_engine, --fetch_mode.

vexy-dexypy analyze https://www.vexy.art/lines/ --aspect 1080p

docs.title: render
docs.text:
Runs stages 4 to 6 for one strategy, using the sidecars of an earlier run. It reads _meta/page.json and _meta/slideplan.json, and uses normalized/normalized.html when that file exists.

Argument or flag Default Meaning SLUG (required) The folder name under --out, for example www-vexy-art-lines STRATEGY (required) One strategy name --out out Output root folder --svg False Also write SVG files --verbose False Debug logging 
vexy-dexypy render www-vexy-art-lines playwright --svg

docs.title: split
docs.text:
Runs stage 6 only on any PDF. It writes 01-slide.pdf, 02-slide.pdf, … and an index.html preview into --out.

Argument or flag Default Meaning PDF (required) Multi-page PDF to split --out . Output folder --svg False Also write SVG files --prefix slide File name part after the number --verbose False Debug logging 
vexy-dexypy split deck.pdf --out slides --prefix page

This writes slides/01-page.pdf, slides/02-page.pdf, and so on.

docs.title: How the slug is made
docs.text:
The output folder name comes from the URL or path. The tool lowercases it, removes a leading http:// or https://, replaces each run of characters other than a–z and 0–9 with -, trims leading and trailing -, and keeps at most 80 characters.

Input Slug https://www.vexy.art/lines/ www-vexy-art-lines https://blog.fontlab.com/ blog-fontlab-com

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Most runs need no configuration file. Flags and defaults cover the common cases. A TOML file lets you fix a house style for a project or for your user account.

docs.title: Where settings come from
docs.text:
vexy-dexypy resolves settings once at startup, in this order of precedence:

  1. Command-line flags.
  2. ./vexy-dexypy.toml in the current folder.
  3. ~/.config/vexy-dexypy/config.toml.
  4. Built-in defaults.

The project file and the user file are merged section by section. Within a section, a key in the project file replaces the same key in the user file.

A file that is not valid TOML stops the run with a usage error that names the file.

docs.title: Example file
docs.text:
# vexy-dexypy.toml
[output]
dir = "out"
svg = false

[stage]
aspect = "720p"          # or "1080p", "810p"
# size = "1600x900"      # overrides aspect when present

[strategies]
enabled = ["playwright", "vivliostyle", "reveal"]   # or "all"

[vision]
enabled = false
model = "minicpm-v-4.6"
endpoint = "http://localhost:11434"

[engines]
prince_path = ""
node_bin = "node"

[browser]
engine = "playwright"    # or "playwrightauthor", "cloakbrowser"

[fetch]
mode = "live"            # or "localize", "offline"
tool = "single-file"     # or "monolith" (offline mode only)

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Section Key Default Flag that overrides it output dir "out" --out output svg false --svg stage aspect none --aspect stage size none --size strategies enabled "all" --strategies vision enabled false --vision vision model "minicpm-v-4.6" — vision endpoint "http://localhost:11434" — engines prince_path "" — engines node_bin "node" — browser engine "playwright" --browser_engine fetch mode "live" --fetch_mode fetch tool "single-file" —

strategies.enabled accepts a TOML list or a comma-separated string.

Note

The Prince exporter currently locates the binary through the VEXY_DEX_PRINCE_PATH environment variable or prince on PATH. The engines.prince_path key is read into the settings but the exporter does not use it yet.

docs.title: Stage size
docs.text:
The stage is the slide rectangle in CSS pixels. The same width and height are used for the browser viewport during analysis, for the @page size in the paged-media CSS, and for the PDF page size in every exporter.

Profile Width × height 720p (default) 1280 × 720 1080p 1920 × 1080 810p 1440 × 810

All three profiles are 16:9. For another shape, give a size such as --size 1024x768. A size wins over an aspect profile. The size string accepts x or × between the numbers, and both numbers must be positive integers.

Errors you can see here:

  • unknown --aspect '4:3'; choose from ['1080p', '720p', '810p'] or pass --size WxH
  • bad --size '1280'; expected WxH like 1280x720 or an --aspect from [...]
  • --size must be positive, got '0x720'

docs.title: Strategy selection
docs.text:
• all runs every exporter registered as a plugin whose available() check passes. The classifier's recommended order comes first; other strategies follow.
  • An explicit list runs exactly those strategies. A name that is not registered stops the run with a usage error. A registered strategy whose program is missing still runs and fails in the summary table with the engine's error message.

The recommended order per page type:

Page type Recommended first webflow playwright, reveal mkdocs-material vivliostyle, playwright docusaurus vivliostyle, playwright framer playwright, reveal bubble playwright, vivliostyle generic vivliostyle, playwright

docs.title: Caching
docs.text:
After an engine writes its combined PDF, the orchestrator stores a copy in out/<slug>/_meta/cache/. The cache key joins the page's content hash, the strategy name and the stage size. On the next run with the same key, the cached PDF is reused and the engine is not called. Pass --no_cache to render again.

Vision results are cached separately in out/<slug>/_meta/vision/, keyed by a hash of the page screenshot and the model name.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: The design contract is the 24-chapter specification in spec/. Read spec/00-tldr.md and CLAUDE.md first. Implement against a chapter; if a change must deviate from it, update that chapter in the same change.

docs.title: Set up a development environment
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository and enter it:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-dexypy.git
cd vexy-dexypy

  2. Install the package with all extras and the dev tools:

    uv sync --extra all

  3. Install Chromium for Playwright:

    uv run playwright install chromium

docs.title: Run the checks
docs.text:
The test suite uses the HTML fixtures in tests/fixtures/ and mocks network calls:

uv run --extra all pytest -v

./test.sh runs ruff check, the tests, and the offline example examples/build_local.py.

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs the tests on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows with Python 3.12 and 3.13, and a lint job with ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples/ folder holds runnable scripts that double as smoke tests. They write to examples/output/, which git ignores.

uv run examples/build_local.py           # offline fixture, no network
uv run examples/webflow_retro_poster.py  # live Webflow page

examples/expected/ holds captured manifests of real output for the live examples.

docs.title: Build the package and the documentation
docs.text:
The root build.sh builds both:

./build.sh            # documentation and package
./build.sh docs       # documentation only, into docs/
./build.sh package    # sdist and wheel into dist/, then twine check

The documentation source is Markdown in src_docs/md/. src_docs/build.sh builds it into docs/ with ProperDocs and the MaterialX theme in strict mode, and src_docs/build.sh serve starts a live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000. GitHub Pages serves docs/ at https://vexy.dev/vexy-dexypy/. The Docs workflow rebuilds docs/ when src_docs/ changes on main.

docs.title: Versions and releases
docs.text:
The version comes from git tags through hatch-vcs. At build time it is written to src/vexy_dexypy/__version__.py, which git ignores, and vexy_dexypy.__version__ reads it.

./publish.sh makes a release:

  1. uvx gitnextver commits pending changes, tags the next vX.Y.Z and pushes.
  2. The script checks that HEAD carries a vX.Y.Z tag.
  3. ./build.sh package builds and checks the distributions.
  4. uv publish uploads them to PyPI. It needs UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN or another uv publish credential.

Pushing the tag also starts .github/workflows/release.yml, which builds the distributions, publishes them to PyPI with trusted publishing (skipping files that already exist), and creates a GitHub release with the matching CHANGELOG.md section.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+, uv for every dependency change.
  • Type hints everywhere; dataclasses for the pipeline types in model.py.
  • Typed errors from vexy_dexypy.errors. A failed strategy is a DeckResult(ok=False), never an aborted run.
  • Every external program call has a timeout and reports its stderr.
  • Each source file carries a this_file comment with its path.
  • Record changes in CHANGELOG.md and new dependencies, with their licences, in DEPENDENCIES.md.

docs.title: Engines
docs.text:
A strategy is a named route from the normalized page to a combined PDF. The strategy name is also the name of its output folder. vexy-dexypy registers six strategies.

Strategy Engine Wrapping (chassis) Available when playwright Chromium page.pdf paged playwright can be imported vivliostyle Vivliostyle CLI paged vivliostyle is on PATH prince PrinceXML paged VEXY_DEX_PRINCE_PATH is set or prince is on PATH reveal reveal.js in Chromium reveal playwright and pypdf can be imported impress impress.js in Chromium impress playwright and pypdf can be imported marp Marp CLI marp (Markdown) marp or npx is on PATH

docs.title: How a strategy runs
docs.text:
For each strategy the orchestrator:

  1. Writes the strategy folder out/<slug>/<strategy>/, with _paged.css (the page size rules) and _theme.css (the cosmetic layer).
  2. Builds the engine input from the normalized HTML: _input.html, or _input.md for Marp.
  3. Calls the engine, which writes _combined.pdf, or copies the cached PDF.
  4. Splits _combined.pdf into 01-slide.pdf, 02-slide.pdf, …, converts them to SVG if requested, and writes index.html.

Strategies run concurrently in worker threads. Strategies that drive a browser share a limit of three at a time. An exception in one strategy becomes a failed row in the summary; the other strategies continue.

docs.title: Paged strategies
docs.text:
The playwright, vivliostyle and prince strategies receive one HTML file with this CSS added before </head> (shown for the 1280×720 stage):

@page { size: 1280px 720px; margin: 0; }
html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; }
* { -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact; }
section, .slide {
  break-after: page;
  page-break-after: always;
  width: 1280px; height: 720px;
  overflow: hidden; box-sizing: border-box;
}
section h2 { break-before: page; page-break-before: always; }

Each <section> becomes at least one page. Content that does not fit is clipped by overflow: hidden.

The cosmetic layer depends on the page type. Webflow and Framer pages keep their own CSS and only hide the "Made in Webflow" badge. All other pages get a small neutral theme: 4% padding, a system sans-serif font, and light or dark slide backgrounds.

docs.title: playwright
docs.text: Opens the input in Chromium at the stage size, switches to screen media, and prints with page.pdf at the exact stage size, with backgrounds and zero margins. The result is close to a vector screenshot of each slide. This is usually the best choice for designed, script-heavy pages.

docs.title: vivliostyle
docs.text:
Runs:

vivliostyle build _input.html -s 1280px,720px -o _combined.pdf

with a 180-second timeout. Vivliostyle has strong CSS paged-media support and suits long-form and documentation pages. It is AGPL-licensed; vexy-dexypy only calls it as a separate program.

docs.title: prince
docs.text: Runs the Prince binary with --page-size=1280px 720px and a 180-second timeout. Prince is proprietary and opt-in: it is used only if you set VEXY_DEX_PRINCE_PATH or put prince on PATH.

docs.title: reveal
docs.text: Wraps the sections in a reveal.js deck that uses the reveal.js copy shipped inside the package, so no network is needed. Chromium opens the deck, waits until Reveal.getTotalSlides() reports at least one slide, then prints one PDF page per slide while stepping with Reveal.next(). pypdf merges the pages into _combined.pdf. This replaces DeckTape and needs no Node toolchain.

docs.title: impress
docs.text: Works the same way with the bundled impress.js: it waits for #impress .step elements, prints one page per step, and moves with impress().next().

docs.title: marp
docs.text:
Translates the normalized HTML into Marp Markdown (_input.md) and runs:

marp --pdf _input.md -o _combined.pdf --allow-local-files --no-stdin

If marp is not installed but npx is, it runs npx -y @marp-team/marp-cli with the same arguments.

docs.title: Engine errors
docs.text:
Program-based engines (vivliostyle, prince, marp) report one of these messages in the summary table:

  • engine not found: <program> (...): the program is not on PATH.
  • <program> timed out after <N>s
  • <program> failed: <last 500 characters of stderr>

Browser-based engines report playwright export failed: …, reveal export failed: … or impress export failed: … with the underlying Playwright error.

docs.title: SVG output
docs.text: With --svg, each single-page PDF is converted with vexy_pdfsvgpy.pdf_to_svg. The preview index.html then shows the SVG files instead of embedding the PDFs. If vexy-pdfsvgpy is not installed, or a conversion fails, the run logs a warning and keeps the PDFs.

docs.title: Extending
docs.text: Readers, importers and exporters are plugins. vexy-dexypy finds them through Python entry points, so another package can add one without changing vexy-dexypy itself.

docs.title: Entry-point groups
docs.text:
Group Plugin returns Selected by vexy_dexypy.readers a reader highest can_read(source) score (in localize mode) vexy_dexypy.importers an importer name equal to the classified page type, else generic vexy_dexypy.exporters an exporter name listed in --strategies, or all with available() true

Each entry point names a class. vexy-dexypy calls it with no arguments to create the plugin. A plugin that fails to load is skipped and logged at DEBUG level.

The built-in plugins are registered in vexy-dexypy's own pyproject.toml:

[project.entry-points."vexy_dexypy.exporters"]
playwright = "vexy_dexypy.exporters.playwright:PlaywrightExporter"
vivliostyle = "vexy_dexypy.exporters.vivliostyle:VivliostyleExporter"
reveal = "vexy_dexypy.exporters.reveal:RevealExporter"

docs.title: Exporter contract
docs.text:
An exporter has three attributes and two methods:

from pathlib import Path

from vexy_dexypy.model import RenderJob


class MyExporter:
    name = "mine"                  # strategy name and output folder name
    needs_js = False               # True: counts toward the 3-browser limit
    supports_paged_media = True

    def available(self) -> bool:
        """Return True when the engine's dependencies are present."""
        return True

    def export(self, job: RenderJob, out: Path) -> Path:
        """Render job.html_path to a multi-page PDF at `out` and return `out`."""
        ...
        return out

The RenderJob gives you:

  • job.html_path: the prepared input file.
  • job.plan.stage_w and job.plan.stage_h: the page size in CSS pixels.
  • job.extra_css: a list holding the path of _paged.css.
  • job.page and job.strategy: the source page and the strategy record.

Raise vexy_dexypy.errors.ExportError with a clear message on failure. For external programs, vexy_dexypy.exporters._subprocess.run_engine(cmd, timeout=…) runs the command with a timeout and turns missing programs, timeouts and non-zero exits into ExportError.

The orchestrator maps strategy names to a chassis (the input format). Names it does not know get the reveal chassis, so a new exporter receives a reveal.js deck as _input.html.

Register the class in your package:

[project.entry-points."vexy_dexypy.exporters"]
mine = "my_package.exporter:MyExporter"

docs.title: Importer contract
docs.text:
from vexy_dexypy.model import PageDoc, SlidePlan
from vexy_dexypy.settings import Settings


class MyImporter:
    name = "my-framework"

    def detect(self, page: PageDoc) -> float:
        """Confidence 0..1 that this importer fits the page."""
        return 0.0

    def transform(
        self, page: PageDoc, plan: SlidePlan, settings: Settings | None = None
    ) -> PageDoc:
        """Return a PageDoc whose html_path points at slide-shaped HTML."""
        ...

vexy_dexypy.importers._common.write_normalized(page, html) writes the HTML to out/<slug>/normalized/normalized.html, fixes asset paths, and returns the updated PageDoc. The helpers in vexy_dexypy.dom (parse, drop_chrome, sectionize, head_styles, wrap_neutral) cover common DOM work.

An importer is chosen by name, and names come from the classifier. A new page type therefore also needs a fingerprint rule in vexy_dexypy.classify, which is a change to vexy-dexypy itself.

docs.title: Reader contract
docs.text:
from vexy_dexypy.model import PageDoc, Source
from vexy_dexypy.settings import Settings


class MyReader:
    name = "mine"

    def can_read(self, source: Source) -> float:
        """Confidence 0..1. The built-in static reader returns 0.5."""
        return 0.0

    def read(self, source: Source, settings: Settings) -> PageDoc:
        """Write the page to settings.out_dir / source.slug / "raw" / "index.html"."""
        ...

Readers are ranked only in localize mode. The live and offline modes call their own readers directly.

docs.title: Check that a plugin is found
docs.text:
After installing your package in the same environment, run:

vexy-dexypy build --help

A new exporter appears in the Available strategies: line when its available() returns True, or in the Unavailable (install deps): line otherwise.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: vexy-dexypy is a Python package with a command-line tool. The core install gives you the playwright, reveal and impress strategies. Other strategies need extra programs on your PATH.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or newer.
  • A Chromium build for Playwright. The default live fetch mode, the pagination probe and the browser-driven exporters all use it.

docs.title: Install the package
docs.text:
1. Install the package with uv:

    uv pip install vexy-dexypy

    Or run it without installing:

    uvx vexy-dexypy --help

  2. Install the Chromium browser that Playwright drives:

    playwright install chromium

  3. Check which strategies are available on your machine:

    vexy-dexypy build --help

    The help text ends with a line such as Available strategies: impress, playwright, reveal. and, if some are missing, Unavailable (install deps): ….

docs.title: Optional extras
docs.text:
The package defines these extras in pyproject.toml:

Extra Installs Used for extract trafilatura Article-body extraction in the generic importer's Python fallback pdf pikepdf PDF post-processing vision instructor Vision-model tooling all playwright, trafilatura, pikepdf Everything above except vision

Install an extra with:

uv pip install "vexy-dexypy[all]"

docs.title: Optional external programs
docs.text:
Each of these enables one strategy or feature. A strategy whose program is missing is skipped when you ask for all strategies.

Program Enables How vexy-dexypy finds it vivliostyle (Vivliostyle CLI) vivliostyle strategy vivliostyle on PATH prince (PrinceXML) prince strategy VEXY_DEX_PRINCE_PATH environment variable, then prince on PATH marp (Marp CLI) or npx marp strategy marp on PATH; otherwise npx -y @marp-team/marp-cli single-file or monolith --fetch_mode offline the configured tool on PATH vexy-pdfsvgpy (Python) --svg output importable as vexy_pdfsvgpy Ollama or another server with an /api/chat endpoint --vision [vision] endpoint, default http://localhost:11434

To install the Vivliostyle CLI with npm:

npm install -g @vivliostyle/cli

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-dexypy.git
cd vexy-dexypy

  2. Create the environment with all extras:

    uv sync --extra all
uv run playwright install chromium

  3. Run the tool from the checkout:

    uv run vexy-dexypy --help

The version number comes from the latest git tag (through hatch-vcs), so a checkout without tags reports a development version.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page builds decks from one web page and then from a local file.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• vexy-dexypy installed (see Installation).
  • Chromium installed with playwright install chromium.
  • Network access for the URL example.

docs.title: Build decks from a URL
docs.text:
1. Run build with the URL:

    vexy-dexypy build https://www.vexy.art/lines/

    The tool fetches the page, classifies it, plans the slide breaks at the default 1280×720 stage, and runs every available strategy.

  2. Read the summary table. Each row shows a strategy, a ✓ or ✗, the slide count, and the output folder or the error:

    strategy     result  slides  output / error
playwright   ✓           11  out/www-vexy-art-lines/playwright
reveal       ✓            9  out/www-vexy-art-lines/reveal
2/2 strategies succeeded.

    The slide counts depend on the live page and on which engines you have installed.

  3. Open a strategy's preview, for example out/www-vexy-art-lines/playwright/index.html, to page through its slides.

  4. Pick the best rendering of each slide from the strategy folders. Every folder uses the same numbering: 01-slide.pdf, 02-slide.pdf, and so on.

docs.title: Choose strategies and stage size
docs.text:
Run only two strategies at 1920×1080 and also write SVG files:

vexy-dexypy build https://blog.fontlab.com/ \
    --strategies vivliostyle,playwright --aspect 1080p --svg
  • --strategies takes a comma-separated list. An unknown name stops the run with a usage error that lists the known strategies.
  • --aspect takes 720p, 1080p or 810p. --size 1600x900 sets any other size and overrides --aspect.
  • --svg needs the vexy-pdfsvgpy package. Without it the run logs a warning and keeps the PDFs.

docs.title: Build decks from a local file
docs.text:
A path that does not start with http:// or https:// is read as a local file. The repository ships a small fixture you can use:

vexy-dexypy build tests/fixtures/generic_article/index.html --out out

The static reader copies the file into out/<slug>/raw/ and downloads any remote assets it references.

docs.title: Re-run part of the pipeline
docs.text:
Each stage writes JSON sidecars into _meta/, so you can repeat later stages without fetching again.

  • Re-render one strategy from the existing sidecars:

    vexy-dexypy render www-vexy-art-lines reveal

  • Split an existing PDF into numbered slides with a preview:

    vexy-dexypy split out/www-vexy-art-lines/playwright/_combined.pdf \
    --out out/www-vexy-art-lines/playwright --svg

See Command line for every command and flag.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Run the failing command again with --verbose first. Debug logging shows which reader, importer and strategies were chosen and why a step fell back.

docs.title: A strategy is missing from the run
docs.text:
With --strategies all, only strategies whose available() check passes run. Check the list:

vexy-dexypy build --help

The help ends with Available strategies: … and, when some are missing, Unavailable (install deps): …. Install the program the strategy needs; see Installation.

docs.title: usage error: unknown strategy 'x'; known: [...]
docs.text: A name in --strategies is not registered. Check the spelling against the list in the message. Names are lower case: playwright, vivliostyle, reveal, prince, impress, marp.

docs.title: engine not found: vivliostyle
docs.text:
You asked for vivliostyle explicitly, but the Vivliostyle CLI is not on PATH. Install it:

npm install -g @vivliostyle/cli

The same pattern applies to prince (set VEXY_DEX_PRINCE_PATH or put prince on PATH) and marp.

docs.title: Playwright says the browser executable does not exist
docs.text:
Playwright is installed but its Chromium download is not:

playwright install chromium

With uv run, use uv run playwright install chromium so the browser matches the environment's Playwright version.

docs.title: live mode needs playwright; falling back to localize
docs.text: The default live fetch mode needs Playwright. Without it, the run downloads the page and its assets instead. Install Playwright, or pass --fetch_mode localize to make the choice explicit.

docs.title: The fetched page is almost empty
docs.text: Pages rendered by client-side JavaScript have little text in their HTML. In localize mode, a body with fewer than 500 characters of text makes the static reader re-read the page in headless Chromium. If that also fails, the log shows dynamic escalation failed (...); using static. Use the default live mode for such pages.

docs.title: Fonts or styles are missing in localize mode
docs.text: Asset downloads are best-effort. Each failed asset is logged as asset <url> -> HTTP <code> or failed to localize asset <url>: … and the run continues. The live mode loads assets from the original site and avoids the problem.

docs.title: offline tool 'single-file' not found on PATH; falling back to localize
docs.text: --fetch_mode offline needs the SingleFile CLI. Install it, or set [fetch] tool = "monolith" in vexy-dexypy.toml and install monolith.

docs.title: Slides break in the wrong places
docs.text:
• Try another stage size: --aspect 1080p or --size 1600x900.
  • Compare strategies. Paged engines follow <section> boundaries; reveal and impress take one page per slide of the normalized deck.
  • Inspect the plan with vexy-dexypy analyze <url>, which prints the break offsets, or read _meta/slideplan.json.
  • Try --vision if you run a local vision model.

docs.title: browser preprocessor failed: …; falling back to python sectionizer
docs.text: The in-browser vexy-dexyjs step failed, often because Chromium is not installed. The importer used its Python fallback instead, which can give fewer or different slides. Fix the browser problem and run again with --no_cache.

docs.title: Old output appears after a change
docs.text: Engine PDFs are cached in out/<slug>/_meta/cache/ by content hash, strategy and stage size. Pass --no_cache to render again, or delete the out/<slug>/ folder.

docs.title: svg requested but vexy-pdfsvgpy unavailable
docs.text: --svg needs the vexy-pdfsvgpy package in the same environment. Without it, you still get the PDFs and the preview.

docs.title: vision model unavailable (...); using heuristic plan
docs.text: The vision server at [vision] endpoint (default http://localhost:11434) did not answer. Start the server or drop --vision. When serving MiniCPM-V, turn off its thinking template; otherwise the JSON answer cannot be parsed.

docs.title: Exit code 2
docs.text: No strategy succeeded, no strategy ran, or a read error stopped the run. The summary table and the log show the reason for each strategy.
